headline: Natural Gas And WTI Crude Lead Commodities Downward As Energy Markets Shift
paragraphs: Natural gas prices cratered 5.77 percent on the day and dropped 12.70 percent for the week due to falling weather demand. WTI crude fell 4.65 percent as traders weighed a Gulf supply recovery, despite Brent remaining relatively flat at USD 108.76 as the market assessed Middle East developments.

In precious metals, gold held near support at USD 4156.70 per ounce, down 5.18 percent over the month as yields and oil picked up ahead of the Federal Reserve rate decision, while silver showed resilience with a 4.13 percent weekly gain despite a daily dip. Copper saw modest movement alongside rising inventories and easing supply worries, even as a major US copper mine was greenlit in Arizona.

The euro traded at 1.1240 against the US dollar, maintaining exchange rate stability for Irish businesses importing dollar-denominated raw materials, while broader macroeconomic pressures continued to influence industrial and energy pricing.
